scope: Permanent public terminology for authored wiki copy, bound to the validated current game-reference artifact.

publicTerms.compatibility: Legacy product, repository, package, and provenance identifiers remain readable where required; new authored public copy uses TEAR Music.
Legacy runtime and replay metadata identifiers remain readable for deterministic playback; new authored public copy uses Adaptive Soundtrack.
Legacy catalog, settings, and bookmark identifiers remain readable; current player-facing labels use Music.
Legacy routes, hostnames, query parameters, launchers, and telemetry remain compatibility readers; current labels use Soundtrack Desk.
Legacy training records, route aliases, and persistence keys remain readable; current labels use Training Operations and stay distinct from Soundtrack Desk.
Legacy scenario/replay codecs and TearBench evidence remain readable; current labels use Scenario Console.
Legacy replay routes and edit-decision-list identifiers remain readable; current labels use Replay Editor.
Legacy replay routes and retained evidence remain readable; current labels use Replay Hub.
Legacy evaluation artifacts and report namespaces remain readable; current labels use Game Agent.
Legacy training records and custody identifiers remain readable; current labels use Training Archive.
Legacy event, route, and journal identifiers remain readable; current labels use Run Monitor.
TearBench remains unchanged, including its evidence routes and historical records.

activeRoster.legacyUsePolicy: Retired IDs may appear only in explicit history or migration material; they are not current selectable weapons.

legacyPolicy.history: Immutable historical records may retain their original terminology.
legacyPolicy.compatibility: Compatibility readers, aliases, and migration maps may retain old identifiers when path-scoped, justified, and tested.
legacyPolicy.g6Boundary: This registry is bound to the validated game-reference artifact; the game repository remains the gameplay authority and historical compatibility remains explicit.
